transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-09-14 15:30 PDT
Duration: 56m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Omar V. (Redwood), Sophie Park (CSM) -- Laura Kim (CISO, Northpoint Health), Diego Ramos (Platform Eng), Anika Singh (IT Ops), Tom Bowers (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick security kickoff to align SAML/SCIM onboarding and RBAC least-privilege model; covered SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS/CMK options, audit log delivery, and next steps for a pilot. Customers had constraints around data residency and on-prem HSM for keys; asked for concrete mapping template and timeline.

Topics covered:
- SAML IdP attributes and nameID expectations
- SCIM provisioning cadence and group->role mapping
- RBAC: admin vs service vs read-only slices, just-in-time access patterns
- Audit logs: retention, export paths, and SIEM integration
- Encryption: CMK/KMS and HSM options, key rotation policies
- Data residency and VPC/private deployment tradeoffs

Action items (brief): see metadata action_items for owners/dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off, um we wanted to run through the SAML/SCIM onboarding flow and then spend a chunk on the role matrix and kms questions — is that still the agenda you're looking for?
[00:12] Laura Kim: yes that's perfect - CISO here - main goal is least privilege with auditable logs. We have strict residency rules for patient PII, so wanna confirm where logs and tokens live.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: got it, thanks Laura. Quick note, our platform supports hosted, dedicated and private VPC deployments; for keys we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and envelope encryption. we'll show what it looks like in practice.
[00:37] Diego Ramos: just to flag, we use Okta for SSO and for SCIM. we do group-based provisioning today and want SCIM to keep role-sync 1:1 with our groups.
[00:48] Maya Chen: perfect - okta is common. on the SAML side we typically ask for the metadata xml, the mapping for nameID (email vs persistent id), and any additional attributes like employeeType or department. we can map those into Redwood roles or groups in the SCIM mapping.
[01:05] Anika Singh: do you support JIT provisioning? we'd prefer not to pre-provision every user, only create accounts when they first sign-in.
[01:13] Ravi Patel: yes - we support JIT via SAML plus SCIM group sync; JIT handles the user record creation and SCIM is used to keep group membership consistent. small caveat on permissions timing — if SCIM sync runs on a minute cadence there can be a short window where role assignment isn't yet applied.
[01:32] Tom Bowers: about audits - we need log pushes into our SIEM (we're on Splunk) and immutable audit trail for admin actions. retention must be 7 years for certain records. can you retain that long?
[01:45] Omar Velasquez: our default audit retention is 90 days for hosted, longer retention is available as an add-on or with dedicated/private deployments. for long-term storage we can export logs to your S3 bucket or syslog endpoint. the export is tamper-evident and we can provide signed checksums for archives.
[02:06] Laura Kim: signed checksums sound good. what about encryption at rest? we need to use customer-managed keys for patient data.
[02:15] Ravi Patel: absolutely - we support CMK with KMS integration. for cloud deployments we integrate with customer KMS (e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and for on-prem or higher assurance we support HSM-backed keys. encryption is envelope-based so model weights and token cache get wrapped. small note: key rotation needs coordination; we'll need to rewrap existing archives if you rotate.
[02:39] Diego Ramos: can the KMS be in our account or do you require a provider account?
[02:43] Omar Velasquez: you can manage keys in your own cloud account and provide a key ARN with a cross-account policy. for private on-prem we can do HSM integration via PKCS#11.
[02:54] Anika Singh: for SCIM group->role mapping, what's the recommended pattern? we have teams: platform, analytics, support, triage, and a handful of service accounts.
[03:03] Ravi Patel: common pattern is groups per role: e.g., platform-admin -> Redwood admin role, analytics-read -> read-only embedding access, support-agent -> issue-facing limited token use. service accounts usually get a dedicated service-role with scoped permissions and a TTL to force rotation. we'll provide a template mapping and recommend using group attribute 'displayName' or 'members' depending on provider.
[03:28] Laura Kim: how do you handle least-privilege for model access? some teams just need embedding calls, some need generation.
[03:36] Maya Chen: we expose per-route and per-model keys; you can scope an API token to only embeddings or only generation or even limit by route and rate. RBAC ties to those scopes so roles can be composition of scopes.
[03:49] Diego Ramos: will you be able to show a sample SCIM payload?
[03:52] Ravi Patel: yes i'll attach a sample scim patch and list. i'll also include edge cases — overlapping groups, multiple inheritances, and how we resolve precedence.
[04:03] Tom Bowers: ok about compliance docs, do you have SOC2 and ISO attestation?
[04:08] Sophie Park: yes — we have SOC2 Type II, and an ISO/27001 summary; i'll upload the attestation and a compliance FAQ. we typically provide a redacted report plus a gap summary if needed.
[04:20] Laura Kim: we might request a SOC2 bridge letter for the pilot period.
[04:23] Maya Chen: understood we'll see what legal can provide.
[04:28] Anika Singh: what about admin impersonation / session logging? if someone makes an admin change we need to know who did it and be able to roll back.
[04:36] Omar Velasquez: admin actions are logged with actor id, IP, timestamp, and diff snapshot; there's an admin change API to revert where possible. for critical changes we support approval workflows integrated via webhook so you can gate.
[04:53] Diego Ramos: any latency or cost tradeoffs for dedicated vs hosted when you enable long-term audit export and CMK?
[05:01] Ravi Patel: dedicated typically has predictable throughput and may add minimal extra latency for crypto operations; export and CMK add network egress and KMS calls which are billed; we'll provide a cost estimate based on your QPS.
[05:16] Laura Kim: data residency: our EU tenants must have keys and logs stored in EU. can you guarantee region pinning?
[05:24] Maya Chen: yes, for private or dedicated we can pin to region and ensure logs/keys stay within that region. for hosted we offer regional endpoints and can discuss contractual residency commitments for enterprise contracts.
[05:37] Anika Singh: small question - what about SCIM rate limits? we have 50k users across orgs.
[05:44] Ravi Patel: SCIM has burst handling; for large directories we'll recommend delta sync and group-scoped syncs. 50k is handled by delta and pagination; full bulk imports are done via a temporary bulk endpoint during initial onboarding.
[06:02] Laura Kim: on the RBAC matrix draft, we'll want a column for auditability and another for required SAML attributes. can you include that?
[06:10] Maya Chen: yes, our template will include role name, permissions, SCIM groups, required SAML attributes, expiry/TTL, and justifications for access.
[06:20] Diego Ramos: what about orphaned accounts when people leave? we need auto-deprovision without manual steps.
[06:25] Ravi Patel: SCIM deprovisioning supports active->suspended->deleted lifecycle; we can soft-delete then auto-delete after a retention window. also we support account status mapping to IdP's 'active' attribute.
[06:38] Tom Bowers: any known gaps for healthcare regulations HIPAA?
[06:44] Sophie Park: we're not a HIPAA covered entity but we can sign a BAA and provide controls; we'll need to review a set of policies and possibly a separate contract for PHI processing.
[06:56] Laura Kim: for the pilot we want: 1) SCIM mapping template 2) RBAC draft 3) CMK demo 4) SOC2 docs. can that be done in two weeks?
[07:05] Maya Chen: yes that's feasible — action owners listed. we'll follow up with calendar invites and attach docs.
[07:12] Diego Ramos: also please include an example of the audit export schema so we can map into our Splunk fields.
[07:19] Omar Velasquez: will do, i'll include sample payloads and a splunk HEC ingest example.
[07:26] Laura Kim: thanks all. small nit — sometimes Fireflies transcripts split speakers oddly; apologies if names are off in the recording.
[07:33] Maya Chen: no worries, we captured the key things. recap: Maya send SOC2, Ravi send SCIM mapping and RBAC matrix, Omar prepare CMK demo and audit export sample, Laura share Okta metadata. we'll meet next Tuesday to review.
[07:50] (crosstalk)
[07:57] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash) and proper nouns may be slightly off. timestamps approximate and represent periodic markers rather than exact token-level timing.
